subject: history

moments.title: Henry's 'Great Matter' begins
moments.who: Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon
moments.body: Henry, having no male heir from Catherine, seeks annulment. Pope Clement VII — a prisoner of Catherine's nephew Charles V after the 1527 Sack of Rome — refuses. Cardinal Wolsey fails to deliver and falls in 1529.
moments.takeaway: The English Reformation begins as a dynastic crisis with a geopolitical lock — the Pope cannot defy the Emperor.

moments.title: The Break with Rome
moments.body: January 1533: Henry secretly marries Anne Boleyn. May 1533: Cranmer annuls the Catherine marriage. 1534: Act of Supremacy declares Henry 'Supreme Head' of the Church of England. Thomas More refuses the Oath of Succession and is executed in 1535.

quote.text: The King's good servant, but God's first.

moments.takeaway: The Reformation in England is enacted by Parliament under royal direction — a top-down political settlement rather than a popular religious revival.

moments.title: Dissolution of the Monasteries
moments.who: Thomas Cromwell and the Court of Augmentations
moments.body: Smaller houses dissolved 1536; larger ones 1538-41. Around 800 religious houses closed; over 10,000 monks, nuns and friars displaced. The Pilgrimage of Grace (October 1536) — perhaps 40,000 northern rebels — was suppressed by Henry's broken promises.
moments.takeaway: Crown wealth doubled briefly; most land was sold to gentry buyers, creating a class invested in not reversing the Reformation.

now.title: Five centuries of consequence
now.body: The Church of England remains established. The Royal Supremacy survives in form — the monarch is still Supreme Governor. Catholic emancipation came only in 1829. Eamon Duffy, Diarmaid MacCulloch and Alec Ryrie have produced the modern scholarly synthesis: a slow, contested, top-down change with deep popular reluctance.
now.open_questions: Was the English Reformation Henry VIII's personal project that became something else, or a wider movement Henry rode? The balance has shifted with each generation of historians.

reflection: Personal motives (a male heir, Anne Boleyn, monastic wealth) and structural pressures (Lutheran Reformation, fiscal need, Pope's captivity) collide in 1533-34. Both readings — accident and inevitability — capture part of the truth.
